\[
M = \sum^8_{i=1} \sum^7_{j=1} (|a_{i,j+1} - a_{i,j}| + |a_{j+1,i} - a_{j,i}|).
\]
Find the remainder when the maximum possible value of $M$ is divided by $1000.$

content:
For an \(8\times 8\) board every cell is adjacent only to cells of the opposite colour in a chessboard colouring.  
Let the black squares be \(B\) and the white squares be \(W\).

For an edge joining a black cell \(b\) and a white cell \(w\)

\[
|a_{w}-a_{b}|=\begin{cases}
 a_{w}-a_{b},& a_{w}>a_{b}\\[2pt]
 a_{b}-a_{w},& a_{b}>a_{w}
\end{cases}
\]

If every white number is larger than every black number, each edge contributes  
\(a_{w}-a_{b}\). Then

\[
M=\sum_{w\in W}\deg(w)\,a_{w}-\sum_{b\in B}\deg(b)\,a_{b},
\]

where \(\deg(v)\) is the degree of vertex \(v\) (the number of its adjacent cells).

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 1.   Degrees of the squares  

* Corners: degree \(2\) – there are \(4\) of them, \(2\) black and \(2\) white.  
* Edge (non‑corner): degree \(3\) – there are \(24\) of them, \(12\) black and \(12\) white.  
* Interior: degree \(4\) – there are \(36\) of them, \(18\) black and \(18\) white.

Thus for the coefficients in the expression for \(M\)

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{colour} & \text{coefficients}\\ \hline
\text{black} & -2\;(2\text{ times}),\; -3\;(12\text{ times}),\; -4\;(18\text{ times})\\
\text{white} & +2\;(2\text{ times}),\; +3\;(12\text{ times}),\; +4\;(18\text{ times})
\end{array}
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 2.   Choosing the numbers  

The sum \(M\) is linear in the placed numbers.  
To maximise it we assign the **smallest** numbers to the most negative
coefficients and the **largest** numbers to the most positive coefficients.

\[
\begin{aligned}
&-4 \text{ (18 squares)}: && 1,2,\dots ,18 &&\text{sum}=171,\\
&-3 \text{ (12 squares)}: && 19,20,\dots ,30 &&\text{sum}=294,\\
&-2 \text{ (2 squares)}: && 31,32 &&\text{sum}=63,\\[4pt]
&+2 \text{ (2 squares)}: && 33,34 &&\text{sum}=67,\\
&+3 \text{ (12 squares)}: && 35,36,\dots ,46 &&\text{sum}=486,\\
&+4 \text{ (18 squares)}: && 47,48,\dots ,64 &&\text{sum}=999 .
\end{aligned}
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 3.   Computing the maximal sum  

\[
\begin{aligned}
M_{\max}&=
(+2)(67)+(+3)(486)+(+4)(999) \\
&\quad -\big[(-4)(171)+(-3)(294)+(-2)(63)\big] \\[2pt]
&= 134+1458+3996\;-\;( -684-882-126)\\
&= 5588-1692\\
&= 3896 .
\end{aligned}
\]

The assignment described above (small numbers on all black squares,
large numbers on all white squares, respecting the degree‑based
distribution) indeed realises this value, so it is the maximum possible
\(M\).

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 4.   Required remainder  

\[
3896\equiv 896 \pmod{1000}.
\]

\[
\boxed{896}
\]
